reading.title: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
reading.passage: Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing the healthcare industry by enabling faster and more accurate diagnoses. Machine learning algorithms can analyze medical images and detect diseases like cancer earlier than traditional methods. AI-powered systems also assist in drug discovery, reducing the time and cost of developing new medications. However, concerns about data privacy and the need for human oversight remain critical challenges. Healthcare professionals must balance technological advancement with patient safety and ethical considerations.

questions.q: According to the passage, what is one benefit of using AI in healthcare?
options: It completely eliminates the need for doctors
It can detect diseases like cancer earlier than traditional methods
It guarantees all medications will be safe
It removes all privacy concerns
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'Machine learning algorithms can analyze medical images and detect diseases like cancer earlier than traditional methods'라고 명시되어 있습니다. AI가 전통적인 방법보다 더 빨리 암 같은 질병을 감지할 수 있다는 것이 주요 이점입니다.

questions.q: What does the passage indicate about challenges in AI healthcare implementation?
options: There are no challenges at all
Only patients are concerned about the technology
Data privacy and need for human oversight are critical challenges
AI cannot help with drug discovery
questions.explanation: 'However, concerns about data privacy and the need for human oversight remain critical challenges'라는 문장에서 데이터 프라이버시와 인간의 감시가 중요한 도전과제임을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Healthcare is becoming outdated
AI has both significant benefits and important ethical considerations in healthcare
Doctors should be replaced entirely by AI systems
Privacy is not important in medicine
questions.explanation: 본문은 AI의 장점(빠른 진단, 약물 개발)과 동시에 도전과제(프라이버시, 윤리적 고려)를 모두 제시하고 있으므로, AI가 의료에서 이점과 고려사항을 모두 가지고 있다는 것이 주요 내용입니다.

writing.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the statement that social media has more negative effects than positive effects on society?

structure.intro: 명확한 입장 제시: 'I agree/disagree that social media has more negative effects on society because...' 형태로 서론을 시작하며, 2-3개의 주요 이유를 preview합니다.
structure.body1: 첫 번째 주요 포인트: 소셜 미디어의 정신 건강에 미치는 부정적 영향 (스트레스, 우울증, 자존감 저하) 또는 긍정적 영향 (연결, 커뮤니티) 중 입장에 맞게 선택하여 구체적 예시 제시
structure.body2: 두 번째 주요 포인트: 소셜 미디어의 정보 확산 (잘못된 정보/가짜뉴스) 또는 긍정적 정보 공유와 사회 운동에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명
structure.conclusion: 입장 재확인 및 전체 논의 요약: 'In conclusion, I believe that social media...' 형태로 마무리하며 사회에 미치는 총체적 영향 재언급

useful_phrases: However, it is important to note that...

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer to work in a large corporation with many employees. Others prefer to work in a small company with few employees. Which do you prefer and why?
useful_expressions: In my opinion, I prefer working in a small company because...
One reason is that small companies offer more opportunities for personal growth and direct impact.
Another advantage is that the work environment is more collaborative and interpersonal relationships are stronger.
For example, in my previous experience...
To summarize my point, I believe that...
sample_points: 소규모 회사에서는 더 다양한 업무 경험을 할 수 있고 직원의 기여도가 더 명확하게 인정받을 수 있다는 점
대규모 기업에서는 더 많은 자원, 체계적인 교육 프로그램, 경력 발전 기회와 안정적인 급여가 있다는 점

listening.title: University Library Research Session
listening.script: Student: Professor Chen, I'm starting my research paper on climate change, but I'm overwhelmed by the amount of information available. Where should I start? Professor Chen: That's a common challenge. First, I recommend using our university library's database. It has peer-reviewed articles that are more reliable than general internet searches. Student: That sounds helpful. How do I access it? Professor Chen: You can log in with your student ID from any campus computer or remotely from home. I also suggest starting with recent review articles to get an overview of the topic. They usually cite other important papers. Student: Oh, that's a smart approach! Should I take notes on everything I read? Professor Chen: No, be selective. Read the abstract first to see if the article is relevant. Only read the full paper if it's directly related to your topic. This will save you time and help you focus on quality sources.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this conversation?
options: The professor is teaching a climate change class
The student is asking the professor for guidance on starting a research paper
They are discussing the university's computer system
The professor is recommending published books about climate
questions.explanation: 대화에서 학생이 교수에게 연구 논문을 어떻게 시작할지에 대해 조언을 구하고 있습니다. 교수는 도서관 데이터베이스 사용법과 효율적인 자료 검색 방법을 제시하고 있습니다.

questions.q: According to Professor Chen, what should students do before reading a full research paper?
options: Contact the author of the paper
Read the introduction section first
Read the abstract to check if it's relevant to their topic
Discuss it with classmates
questions.explanation: 교수는 '먼저 abstract를 읽어서 논문이 자신의 주제와 관련이 있는지 확인한 후, 직접 관련이 있을 경우에만 전체 논문을 읽으라'고 조언했습니다.

questions.q: What advantage of using review articles does the professor mention?
options: They are shorter and easier to read
They usually cite other important papers and provide an overview of the topic
They are written by famous authors
They are available in print format only
questions.explanation: 교수는 review 논문을 먼저 읽으면 주제에 대한 개요를 얻을 수 있고, 다른 중요한 논문들을 인용하고 있어서 추가 자료를 찾는 데 도움이 된다고 설명했습니다.
